witchetty-grub.name: Witchetty grub
witchetty-grub.summary: Large, white, wood-eating moth larvae eaten in Australia, historically a staple food in the diets of Aboriginal Australians.

quandong.name: Quandong
quandong.summary: Common name mainly for Santalum acuminatum, a desert tree species valued especially for its edible fruit.

backhousia-citriodora.name: Lemon myrtle
backhousia-citriodora.summary: A flowering plant native to subtropical Queensland, Australia, valued as a lemon-scented spice.

tetragonia-tetragonioides.name: Warrigal greens
tetragonia-tetragonioides.summary: A leafy flowering plant native to eastern Asia, Australia and New Zealand, often cultivated as a vegetable; it grows well on sandy, salty coastal ground.

fire-stick-farming.name: Fire-stick farming
fire-stick-farming.summary: Cultural burning practice used by Aboriginal Australians for thousands of years to manage vegetation, aid hunting, and increase biodiversity.

araucaria-bidwillii.name: Bunya pine
araucaria-bidwillii.summary: A large coniferous tree native to southeast Queensland, Australia, with a tallest known individual of 51.5 metres in Bunya Mountains National Park.

fistulina-hepatica.name: Beefsteak fungus
fistulina-hepatica.summary: An edible bracket fungus that visually resembles a slab of meat, found in Europe, Africa, Australia and North America.

malleefowl.name: Malleefowl
malleefowl.summary: Stocky, chicken-sized Australian ground bird known for the large nesting mounds males build and for giving no care to chicks after they hatch.

yamatji.name: Yamatji
yamatji.summary: A Wajarri word for a member of the Wajarri people, or more broadly any Aboriginal Australian from the Murchison region of Western Australia.

yol-u.name: Yolŋu
yol-u.summary: Aboriginal Australian people of north-eastern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, whose clans belong to either the Dhuwa or Yirritja moiety.

walu-goddess.name: Walu
walu-goddess.summary: A sun deity of the Yolŋu people of Arnhem Land, said to light a fire each morning, paint herself with red ochre, and carry a torch across the sky from east to west.
